description: Convxy 1.9 — Liquid Glass across the interface. The glass system now covers the controls, not just the chrome: switches, sliders, buttons, pills, the nav bar, the mini player, the player's own transport and volume controls, and long-press menus are real backdrop-sampling glass — each surface records the pixels behind it, blurs and refracts them through a lens, edge-lights them and answers touches with springs. A menu opened over the player bends the album art through its body; nothing is a translucent colour painted on top.

changelog.title: Liquid Glass controls
items: Switches and sliders join the glass system: the liquid slider keeps the original capsule thumb that swells on press, with press-animated blur, lens and inner shadow on springs. It is opt-in as SliderStyle.LIQUID and switches on automatically with glass; every previous slider style remains available.

Buttons, icon buttons, segmented pills and tabs, circular queue buttons and the volume slider rows render as glass: sampled backdrop, blur, refraction, edge highlight and shadow, with spring press feedback.
The bottom navigation bar, mini player and floating now-playing pill sit on the shared backdrop recording, so they refract whatever scrolls beneath them.
Player transport controls, the seek bar and its thumb, and the volume rail refract the player's own background — the artwork wash, not the page behind the sheet.

changelog.title: Glass menus and sheets
items: Long-press menus render as a liquid glass sheet: the sheet body blurs and refracts what is actually under it — the player's exported glass surface (artwork included) while the player is open, the page stack otherwise — and the rows and pills inside the menu sample the sheet's own painted surface.
The queue sheet's header pills and circular buttons, and the player's bottom device/sleep-timer/comments trio, refract the player background through the same exported recording.
Dialogs and bottom-sheet pages route through the same backdrop providers, so their surfaces stay glass-consistent with the rest of the app.

changelog.title: The engine under it
items: Surfaces sample recorded layers, not live captures: the app root records the page stack, the player records its background subtree and exports it, and each glass surface draws the recording cropped to its bounds. An ancestry guard refuses cyclic samplings, with a frosted fallback so the UI never breaks.

Effect pipeline per surface: vibrancy, runtime shader blur scaled against radius for performance, lens refraction with chromatic aberration, edge highlight, shadow and inner shadow, tint — all spring-animated on press.

Settings expose the master glass toggle, blur radius, vibrancy, lens depth, refraction, noise, tint, corner shape, springs, slider style and rubber-band overscroll; turning glass off restores the previous Material surfaces exactly.

changelog.title: Documentation and credit
items: docs/LIQUID_GLASS.md documents the recording/sampling model, the component list, the settings and the rules for putting glass on a new surface.
The engine vendors Kyant0/AndroidLiquidGlass (Apache-2.0) with attribution headers kept; the glass system design descends from Convx (GPL-3.0). Convxy remains GPL-3.0.
